subject: Technical discovery recap & VPC endpoint checklist
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery call follow-up: constraints & questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciate the runthrough of Redwood's runtime and deployment options. A quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups we didn't get to:

- Goal: integrate a patient-facing summarization/insights feature into BrightBridge's provider portal. Latency target ~300ms p50 for short prompts, and embeddings/reranker for semantic search.
- Connectivity constraints: must use our VPC-only egress (no public internet), prefer VPC endpoint or PrivateLink, IP allowlist on our side for any outgoing connections, and support for mTLS to mutual-authenticate services.
- Auth: We plan to use short-lived service identities; interested in SDK guidance for rotating credentials and support for customer-managed certs (HSM-backed) if mTLS is required.
- Routing: traffic must egress via our NAT and through internal DNS. Do you support custom DNS entries for private endpoints?
- Structured output: we plan to use function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs. Can Redwood pin models and provide stable output schema enforcement or validation hooks?
- Embeddings/rerankers: want to know best practices for batching and embedding storage (we use Aurora + Redis cache).

Can you send a short architecture sketch and a checklist of next steps we should prepare for a Private deployment (VPC endpoint, firewall rules, certs, logging)? Also, availability for a 45-minute technical deep-dive next week (Jan 18–20)?

Thanks,

Alex Chen
Infrastructure Lead
BrightBridge Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery call follow-up: constraints & questions

Hi Alex — great speaking with you and the BrightBridge team. Below is a concise post-call recap and immediate next steps. I've attached a short checklist and a quickstart for the Redwood SDK.

Recap / confirmations from the call:
- Private connectivity: Redwood supports Private deployments with VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) or VPC peering depending on cloud provider. For strict "no public egress" we recommend our VPC endpoint + NAT egress through the customer VPC.
- IP allowlist: we can publish stable egress IP ranges for the Dedicated/Private deployment you choose; for Hosted endpoints we rely on customer VPC networking.
- mTLS & certs: we support mTLS in Private deployments. Customer-presented client certs (mutual TLS) are supported for Enterprise customers and require onboarding to our cert management flow (we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for key material at rest).
- Auth & SDK: recommended pattern is short-lived JWTs issued by your identity provider; our SDK has helpers for token refresh and transparently reauthenticating. See snippet below for the node quickstart.

SDK snippet (Node, pseudocode):
const client = new RedwoodClient({ endpoint: 'https://private.redwood.example', auth: getShortLivedToken() });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Summarize patient note' });

Routing & DNS:
- We support custom private DNS zones for PrivateLink endpoints so your internal DNS names can resolve to the private endpoint.
- Egress will flow through your NAT; we'll provide a recommended set of firewall rules and NACLs.

Structured output / tool-calling:
- Function/tool calling is supported. We recommend anchoring schema validation client-side and using our output validators for strong enforcement. We can pin model versions for you at deploy time to reduce regression risk.

Embeddings & rerankers:
- Use batched embedding calls (size ~64–256 depending on model) and cache embeddings in Redis. For reranking, we suggest a hybrid approach: ANN index for candidate recall + Redwood reranker for final ordering.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share an architecture sketch from your infra team (or we can draft one) — I attached a checklist to guide inputs.
2) Schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive Jan 18 or 19 (we're available 10–2 PT).
3) If you need customer-managed certs or Dedicated capacity, we'll scope an onboarding timeline (typical lead >2 weeks for cert exchange + network review).

Attachments: jb-integration-checklist.pdf, redwood_sdk_quickstart.md

Links: HubSpot deal and a sample arch folder sent separately.

Thanks — looping in Aisha to confirm mTLS cert workflow and Rishi for Dedicated capacity notes.

— Jordan

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from the infra team: 

- Can you confirm whether customer-managed certs means we provide the private key or whether Redwood will hold the key material (we prefer KMS/HSM retention on our side if possible)?
- For audit/logging: will we be able to ingest request logs (token-anonymized) into our SIEM or do you push logs to us? Any options for streaming audit logs to a customer-owned S3 or Pub/Sub?
- Data residency: our PHI processing must be in us-east-1. Does Redwood guarantee region pinning for Private deployments?
- SLA/throughput: if we go Dedicated for low latency, what are typical p50/p95 latencies for request sizes ~512 tokens?

We can do Jan 19 at 11:00 PT for the technical deep-dive — please send calendar invite.

Alex

Subject: Internal: BBH mTLS/certs + Dedicated feasibility (internal action items)

Aisha / Rishi — internal follow-up from the BrightBridge thread. Alex has asked three things we should confirm before the Jan 19 call:

1) Customer-managed certs: can we support the customer holding private key material in their KMS/HSM and perform mutual TLS without Redwood ever seeing the private key? If not fully supported, what's our minimal exposure and required steps for secure exchange?
2) Audit log delivery: product options for streaming anonymized request logs to customer-owned S3 or pushing syslog to a collector. Need a short doc on retention windows and PII handling.
3) Region pinning & Dedicated latency: estimate p50/p95 numbers for 512-token requests on Dedicated in us-east-1; include scaling guidance for 200 concurrent users (avg QPS 5–10).

Action items:
- Aisha: write up cert/KMS patterns + compliance notes (target: 48 hours).
- Rishi: provide Dedicated sizing + latency expectations and an estimated onboarding timeline (target: 72 hours).
- I'll prepare a short architecture sketch to send to BBH prior to the Jan 19 call and draft the calendar invite.

We should avoid promising customer-held private keys unless we confirm the protocol — likely we can do an mTLS proxy where customer certs terminate in their VPC and we authenticate based on mutual-proxy token exchange. Confirm specifics.

— Jordan

Redwood Inference
